definition: In this context, marginal frequency refers to a summary of how neural response activity is distributed across sound frequencies, used to compare tuning patterns from different signal types. It captures the frequency-related part of a spectro-temporal response while leaving out the time dimension.

reasons: The packet mentions “marginal frequency distributions” but does not define “marginal frequency” as a summary across sound frequencies, nor state that it “leaves out the time dimension.”

The definition’s comparison purpose (to compare tuning patterns from different signal types) is not explicitly stated in the packet for the term itself; the packet describes comparisons of marginal frequency distributions between spike-based and LFP-based signals but does not provide a definitional statement of what the term means.

The packet supports that marginal frequency distributions are used in comparisons between spike-based STRFs and filtered LFPs, but it does not define the term as a general summary of neural response activity across sound frequencies.

The claim that it "captures the frequency-related part of a spectro-temporal response while leaving out the time dimension" is an unsupported extrapolation; the source only says the comparisons were made "on the basis of their marginal frequency distributions."
